To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the best features are those that capture the semantic relatedness of question-answer pairs, followed by features that model the social network structure, and then features that capture the textual similarity of questions and answers; (ii) the best algorithmic approach is the learning to rank one, which outperforms other methods such as the one based on the ranking SVM; (iii) the most promising topic for the best answer prediction task is the one that contains questions about computers and technology, followed by

(i) the best answer prediction task is a complex process that can be tackled from different dimensions, (ii) a learning to rank approach that uses the most comprehensive set of features to date outperforms the state of the art by a large margin, and (iii) a novel family of features based on distributional semantics can be used in lieu of the most commonly used linguistic similarity measures, providing better performance in a fraction of the time.

(1) the use of distributional semantics features can replace linguistic features with a better predictive power, (2) the use of a learning-to-rank framework with a large number of diverse features can improve the accuracy of question-answ- er matching by 11-26p, and (3) the best features are topic-dependent.
